_comment: Sweep routers (#693/PR #711): a lone player Cavalry ('Sweeper', uid 0) sits between two enemy targets. 'Holdout' (uid 3) is a full-strength Infantry that closes on a player Spearmen tie-down ('Anvil') and stays FIGHTING it -- close to the sweeper (~140-150 px) but never routs. 'Fleeing' (uid 4) is a weak, low-morale Infantry spawned in contact with a second player Cavalry ('Breaker'); it takes until ~tick 50 to cross the rout threshold (its starting morale is low but not zero), then ROUTS and flees. Giving the sweeper the SWEEP_ROUTERS stance (Ctrl+,) makes it lock onto Holdout at first (nothing is routing yet), then switch onto Fleeing the moment it starts routing (~tick 55-60), bypassing the closer, still-fighting Holdout -- the actual re-targeting choice under test. Because Breaker keeps pursuing under its own Hold order, Fleeing is run down and fully annihilated by ~tick 85-90, at which point the sweeper reverts to Holdout (the only enemy left in range) for the remainder of the run. Verified by state dump: target_enemy_uid is null at tick 10, 3 (Holdout) at tick 40, 4 (Fleeing) at tick 70 -- inside the router-priority window -- then 3 again from tick 100 onward once Fleeing is gone.

shape_residual.reason: Uid 4 (the 30-man unit meant to rout) chases team 0's second Cavalry (uid 2) at up to a sprint, in and out of the fight, with its grid folded about 90 degrees from its facing. The fold is not the cause: a probe of a lone 30-man block in such a swinging chase gives no larger a residual folded than square. Two mechanisms drive it, measured 2026-10-30 on Windows. While the engaged latch outlives each brush with the enemy, its front rank is the engaged body tier, which drops the march feed-forward, and the anchor follows that rank, so the anchor moves at about half the march speed the other men are fed (in the probe the latch takes the worst residual from 7.3 to 15.7 at fold 0); this is tracked in #1887. And it leaves each brush scrambled and marches on so (#1837). The clip itself needs re-staging (#1753: it no longer shows a router or a retarget). Dense 2-tick FULL dumps judged with no exemption against 13.5: main b1d5822b reads 22.2, 17.0, 18.1, 22.0 and 19.8 on seeds 0 to 4, on 16b003c7 (#1847 and #1878) 18.7, 18.2, 21.7, 21.1 and 19.3; and on e57be4c6 (#1880, measured 2026-11-01) 23.87, 22.41, 20.88, 23.66 and pass, against 9f9bddee's 18.72, 18.21, 21.75, 21.06 and 19.33. Remove this exemption once #1887 and #1837 have landed and the clip is re-staged (#1753).

overlap.reason: Uid 4, overlap: Dense 2-tick FULL dumps, every exemption removed, Windows, seeds 0 to 4, against 2.25: 9f9bddee reads pass, pass, pass, 0.28, pass; e57be4c6 (#1880) reads 0.76, 0.41, pass, 1.33, pass. Traced on seeds 0, 1 and 3 on e57be4c6 and on 9f9bddee: the 30-man block chases uid 2 in and out of contact, and each judged dip is out of contact on its ATTACK march just after a brush, with its men 20 to 25 wu off their slots (median) and the farther man of the pair 27 to 43 wu off his: worst at ticks 220, 236 and 238 here (last contact at ticks 214, 210 and 214), and at tick 226 on 9f9bddee's seed 3 (0.28, the farther man 40.5 wu off, last contact at tick 210). Men of a block that leaves a brush scrambled (#1837) walk back across it, and a man walking back from farther off passes through one nearer his slot (#1894): the same-unit standoff now runs while they stand off their slots, but at its gentle push it does not hold off a man closing at the pace of this chase. Measured 2026-11-01.
